Resume

Senior Drupal and React Developer

Building for the web since 1995 and working with Drupal since 2010. I'm strongest on the front-end and on Drupal module work, and I'm at my best inside a team. I help maintain Easy Breadcrumb, a Drupal navigation module that ships with Drupal CMS and is used on more than 115,000 sites.

Technical Skills

  • Drupal: Drupal 6-11, Symfony, Plugin API, Configuration Management, Dependency Injection and Service Containers, Entity and Cache APIs, Drush, JSON:API, Recipes
  • Testing: Static, unit, kernel, functional, and end-to-end testing using PHPUnit, PHPStan, ESlint, PHPCS, CSPELL, Playwright, Behat, Selenium, and many others..
  • Front-end and decoupled: React/Next/Typescript, ES6+, Node.js, Storybook / KSS and living style guides, HTML5, SASS/CSS3
  • Data and platforms: Apache Solr, MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MSSQL migration, Acquia Cloud, AWS, Pantheon, Apache, Nginx, Docker, DDEV, SSH, Bash
  • Accessibility: WCAG

Open Source Work

Credited on 216 resolved Drupal.org issues, plus contributions to security advisories and technical documentation.

  • Easy Breadcrumb - Maintainer. Drupal navigation module that ships with Drupal CMS and is used on more than 115,000 sites.
  • Config Suite - Maintainer. Drupal module that allows for automatic configuration import, export, and exchange between sites.
  • Drupal 8 Multilingual Demo - Core readiness contributions. Contributed to the demonstration project during Drupal Core's alpha and beta cycles, helping prepare Core for multilingual deployment.
  • Drupal AI Learners - Member. Participant in the ecosystem working group on Drupal and AI, collaborating in the official Slack channels on where the community is heading.

Professional Experience

Independent — Open Source & Ecosystem Study | Jun 2023 – Present

  • Planned a three-month break at 46 and extended it to three years. Used the time to study, to volunteer at a local animal rescue, and to plan my future Drupal career trajectory in the quickly-changing age of AI.
  • July-Sept 2026: shipped a release for Easy Breadcrumb extending test coverage to every configuration option, a correctness fix needed by work underway in the Drupal CMS team, and a major bug fix for Config Suite to allow syncing to work for all delete cases.
  • Developed a local containerized AI workflow for safe parallel orchestration of multiple harnesses using DDev and T3Code with spec-driven development using Strikethroo.

Redaptive.com | Staff Software Engineer | Nov 2018 – Jun 2023

  • Started as the sole front-end and Drupal developer and grew the engineering operation into a team, establishing the code standards, Git workflows, and technical documentation the department worked under.
  • Built decoupled React front ends against enterprise Drupal installations on Acquia Cloud, integrated real-time AWS data streams, and worked cross-functionally with an internal Java engineering team.
  • Set up engineering knowledge management and project governance across the Atlassian suite, writing the Confluence documentation and structuring the Jira workflows.

Hook 42 | Senior Drupal Developer | 2015 – 2018

A San Francisco Drupal agency. Client engagements included Zicasso and SunPower.

  • Zicasso.com | Senior Drupal Developer | 2016 – Aug 2018
    • Maintained a high-traffic transactional e-commerce platform connecting global travelers with agencies.
    • Built custom components including automated invoicing and secure internal messaging.
    • Developed a component-driven front-end ecosystem through a living style guide and design pattern library using KSS.
    • Built and ran a custom multivariate A/B testing engine to optimize conversion funnels, using Pantheon Multisite and Google Analytics.
  • SunPower.com | Senior Drupal Developer | 2015 – 2016
    • Led development of the SunPower Savings Calculator, which won the 2016 Oracle Markie Award for Best Web or Commerce Experience.
    • Engineered an internationalized multi-site architecture and streamlined multilingual translation workflows on Acquia.

Thought Matrix | Senior Drupal Developer | Mar 2012 – 2014

A major San Francisco agency, later merged with Rauxa. Client engagements included Johnson & Johnson, General Electric, Fidelity Biosciences, and the University of Phoenix.

  • Alzforum.org (Fidelity Biosciences)
    • Lead developer on the rebuild of a 15-year-old scientific networking platform into a Drupal architecture hosted on Acquia.
    • Migrated the platform off MSSQL with Apache Solr indexing, supporting thousands of users creating their own annotations and comments alongside dozens of PubMed paper-citations, news articles, and reviews published daily.
    • Integrated a third-party vendor's responsive template into a custom theme.
    • Built a custom publishing and review system that pulled nightly scientific updates from PubMed APIs.
  • General Electric (Inside GE Software): Built an internal responsive corporate platform on custom installation profiles, heavily leveraging panels for flexible content editing.
  • University of Phoenix: Worked directly with Acquia teams to launch an agile, responsive research portal for research fellows on aggressive timelines.
  • Johnson & Johnson: Engineered mobile-responsive Drupal sites for One Touch diabetes testers and Children With Diabetes, building multi-step AJAX-driven forms with custom Google Analytics tracking funnels.

Bella Pictures | Drupal Developer | Dec 2011 – early 2012

Wedding photography and video company owned by Sears, hired through Robert Half recruiting.

item.title: Testing with DDev, Gitlab, and serving Drupal from a subfolder instead of a subdomain
item.description:
Testing with DDev, Gitlab, and serving Drupal from a subfolder instead of a subdomain

While working on the Easy Breadcrumb module for Drupal, I came across a situation where a test was failling on Gitlab but was passing with DDev: https://www.drupal.org/project/easy_breadcrumb/issues/3615550

The difference that mattered was that Gitlab serves the site from http://localhost/web for testing and locally it gets served from a fully qualified domain name, ie. http://ddev.site.example.com.

Getting the test to fail locally

Using firecow/gitlab-ci-local

To get the test to fail locally, I used the suggestions at https://project.pages.drupalcode.org/gitlab_templates/info/test-locally/ , which suggested firecow/gitlab-ci-local . I did get that working but I ran into a hitch. My work computer is a Mac with an ARM64 chip and gitlab-ci-local tries to install selenium/standalone-chrome:127.0, which doesn't support ARM64. I dug around and figured out that I could use selenium/standalone-chromium:latest instead by adding a few lines in .gitlab-ci.yml:

phpunit:
  services:
    - !reference [.with-database]
    - name: selenium/standalone-chromium:latest
      alias: selenium
      
# The lines below are to filter which tests run. In this case, only tests in the
# "redirect" group.
variables:
  _PHPUNIT_TESTGROUPS: "redirect"

Then, on the command line, to just run PHPUnit and not most of the other steps, I used the --stage flag to just run jobs in the test stage, which by default is just PHPUnit:

$ drupal-ci-local --stage=test

That worked and I was able to reproduce locally. But, it took about a minute to run the test instead of 2 or 3 seconds with DDev.

Using DDEV to serve a Drupal site from a subdirectory instead of a subdomain

This way is not perfect, but it worked well enough for me to use Xdebug when running tests and when browing the site in a browser.

The code below results in the site being served from a subdirectory named easy, ie. http://example.com/easy.

First, cd to root of project, then:

mkdir router
ls -s ./web ./router/easy

Then, in .ddev/config.yaml

docroot: router

Next, in settings.php

if (isset($GLOBALS['request'])) {
 $request = $GLOBALS['request'];
 $script_name = $request->server->get('SCRIPT_NAME');
 if ($script_name === '/easy/index.php' || $script_name === '/index.php') {
   $request->server->set('SCRIPT_NAME', '/easy/index.php');
 }
}

Then, in .ddev/nginx_full/nginx-site.conf, replace the section that starts with 'location /' to be like this instead:

   # 1. CSS/JS caches
   location ~* ^/easy/sites/.*/files/(css|js)/ {
       try_files $uri @rewrite;
       expires max;
       log_not_found off;
   }
   # 2. Image styles
   location ~* ^/easy/sites/.*/files/styles/ {
       try_files $uri @rewrite;
   }
   # 3. Clean URLs
   location /easy {
       try_files $uri $uri/ /easy/index.php?$query_string;
   }
   # 4. Fallback
   location @rewrite {
       rewrite ^/easy/(.*)$ /easy/index.php?$query_string;
   }

To run phpunit tests, pass in SIMPLETEST_BASE_URL.
Example which just runs ones test:

ddev exec SIMPLETEST_BASE_URL=http://localhost/easy vendor/bin/phpunit --bootstrap web/core/tests/bootstrap.php --filter testEasyBreadcrumbFollowRedirects web/modules/custom/easy_breadcrumb

item.title: Bash scripts for Drupal, DDEV, and Tome
item.description:
Bash scripts for Drupal, DDEV, and Tome

This website is made with Drupal. Local development is done with DDEV configured to use Orbstack for container management. The Tome Drupal module exports the dynamic site to a static site. Python is used to preview the site locally. Public hosting is provided free by Github.

Here are some custom bash aliases and functions I use to make common local tasks easy. Concurrently is used to run two processes in one terminal session.

alias brookemahoneycomCd='cd ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom'
brookemahoneycomLaunch () {
  # Starts Orbstack if it isn't running.
  orb
  brookemahoneycomCd
  cd drupal
  ddev launch
}

brookemahoneycomPreview () {
  brookemahoneycomCd
  cd docs
  concurrently 'python -m http.server' 'open "http://localhost:8000"'
}

brookemahoneycomBuild() {
  # Starts Orbstack if it isn't running.
  orb
  # Changes to the drupal directory.
  cd ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/drupal
  # Clears caches.
  ddev drush cr
  # Exports the site with Tome.
  ddev drush tome:static --uri=https://brookemahoney.com
  # Removes old docs directory.
  rm -rf ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
  # Copies the Tome build directory to docs for Github hosting.
  cp -R ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/drupal/html ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
  # Copies over static files, such as CNAME for Github hosting.
  cp -R ~/projects/brookemahoneycom/sync/ ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
}

All the code for the Drupal install is in this site's Github repo.
